lead.hed: USNI: Lincoln is on track for the second-longest carrier cruise since the Cold War
lead.insight: USNI reported Tuesday that USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) is weeks from a 295-day mark on Sept. 12, which would be the second-longest carrier deployment since the Cold War, behind only USS Gerald R. Ford’s cruise that ended in May. As of Tuesday, Lincoln, its escorts, and Carrier Air Wing 9 were in the Indian Ocean. The Navy has not published a homecoming date.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by NAVCENT Public Affairs · DVIDS 9872029 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · An F-35C Lightning II assigned to Marine Fighter Attack Squadron (VMFA) 314 prepares to launch from USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72), Aug. 11, 2026. Caption must say Aug. 11 5th Fleet file photo, not today’s Indian Ocean position.

political.hed: Defense News: the first North Korea–Russia road bridge is nearly finished
political.insight: Defense News, Wednesday from Vienna: Planet satellite imagery shows the first road bridge across the Tumen River at Tumangang is nearly complete on the North Korean side, including a customs building and a controlled entry. Construction on the Russian approach, the road, and border facilities is still unfinished. No opening date for commercial traffic was published.

political.hed: Defense News: Lincoln is due in Thailand next week
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: a Thai official said Abraham Lincoln will dock in Thailand next week for rest after leaving the Middle East on Saturday. Thailand’s Navy confirmed a U.S. carrier strike group will make a brief stop in the east, with no exercises, and did not name the ships or the date. The U.S. Embassy in Bangkok did not immediately comment.

political.hed: Defense News: ousted Ukraine minister says Kyiv is slowly losing
political.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: former Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov told Reuters Ukraine appears to be slowly losing the war and has a window of several months to change course. Ukraine’s presidential office said he had been positive about the war while he was in the ministry. Fedorov said it was too early to say whether he would run for president.

tech.hed: Defense News: the Navy’s next air-launched torpedo would glide in
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: the Navy is asking industry for Silent Anvil, an air-launched anti-submarine torpedo that glides into the water. One path is a new compact round; the other is a glide kit on an existing torpedo. The request for information closes Sept. 29. A prototype is sought within 18 months of an award. The Navy did not publish a range.

tech.hed: Law & Liberty: Gorsuch’s Slaughter concurrence points past Humphrey’s
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: in Trump v. Slaughter the Court held the president may remove the FTC’s head, overruling Humphrey’s Executor. Justice Neil Gorsuch voted with the majority. His concurrence, which no other justice joined, argues the Court should next return legislative and judicial powers from agencies to Congress and the courts.

culture.hed: WORLD: Scott’s Dog Stars has the landscape, not the focus
culture.insight: WORLD, Tuesday: Ridley Scott’s The Dog Stars, from Peter Heller’s 2012 novel, follows Hig (Jacob Elordi) and Bangley (Josh Brolin) in a virus-emptied 2035 Colorado. The review credits striking mountain photography and says the script turns episodic, with a jarring third-act shift. The film is rated R for language and strong violence.

watch.hed: WATCH: the Marine lab has the first Ancillary Surface Craft
watch.insight: USNI reported Tuesday that the Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory accepted the first of two Ancillary Surface Craft prototypes, citing a lab release last week. The craft is built to move Marines and supplies onto shallow, unimproved shores. The Corps has not said when the second hull arrives, and it has not named a production buy.
